narrative.overview:
psimeter is one instrument world in two Home Screen sizes. The systemSmall widget is an aneroid, a 164 pt square on the reference iPhone 17 Pro. A gunmetal plate with four slotted screws holds a knurled brass bezel and a round dial. The dial carries a shallow five-band enamel arc with one needle, a wide three-wheel roller counter for the 24-hour PSI, a small counter for the WAQI AQI, and engraved legends. Every mark on the face is metal, enamel, glass, a tick or engraved text. There are no buttons, icons, chips or cards. On the Lock Screen, where the materials cannot survive vibrant rendering, the accessories drop to plain system type and make no attempt to imitate brass.

The systemLarge widget is a barograph, 350 × 364 pt on the same phone. The same gunmetal plate, its four brass screws now seated in counterbores, carries a brass drum housing across its upper half. Through the housing window a paper drum shows the last 24 hours of PSI as a pen trace over faint band zones, and a brass pen arm's nib marks the current reading at the right edge of the chart, which is now. Below the drum the plate holds the PSI and AQI roller counters in grained brass frames, and engraving for the legends, the four regional PSIs and the time. The barograph adds the trace and nothing else: the same materials, light and type voices as the aneroid.

The world changes material with the appearance. It never inverts. Day is grained silver, black engraving and a blued-steel needle; on the barograph it is warm chart paper and violet-black pen ink. Night is black lacquer with radium lume: legends, ticks, wheel figures and the barograph's trace glow, the needle turns gunmetal with a lume strip, the paper turns black under a lume grid, and the brass becomes a tone-mapped, darker copy of the day brass. A tinted or clear Home Screen gets a third finish, an open line drawing that keeps the engraved structure and puts the needle, the pen, the trace and the figures in the accent group.

The reading is the product, so the figures carry it and the band supports it. Figures never take the band colour. The band shows only as the needle's position over the enamel, or the pen's position over the chart zones, where the current band is the brightest. The aneroid face is dense, about a dozen engraved strings on 164 pt, and it holds together with two type voices, one light source and a 9 pt floor.
keyCharacteristics: Two instruments in one world: the systemSmall aneroid, drawn in code over three raster textures on a 170 pt grid, and the systemLarge barograph, drawn in code over raster materials on a 350 × 364 pt canvas.
Exact figures on roller wheels; the band arc and the 24-hour trace are supporting cast.
A material switch for night (lacquer, black paper, lume, dimmed brass), never an inverted palette.
Engraved serif for every legend and Archivo Black figures for the two readings. Nothing else is set on either face.
Light from the upper left everywhere: dial sheen, crystal glare, plate bevel, screw bores, needle, hub, pen and counter shadows.
Honest states drawn in the material: blank wheels for missing data, a rust or ember stale mark, a pegged needle, an empty chart engraved `TREND · OFFLINE`.

rules.name: The One Lit Band Rule
rules.body: The segment holding the current PSI draws at full enamel under a 38% white glaze. The other four are muted (22% toward mid-grey by day, 15% toward black by night) under a 22% glaze. With no PSI reading, no segment is lit. The barograph's chart zones obey the same rule: the zone holding the current PSI fills at 30% of its enamel and every other zone at 12% by day and 8.5% at night; the accented finish uses white at 14% and 3%. The zone is lit by the current reading, not by where the trace has been.

rules.name: The Figures Never Take the Band Rule
rules.body: Wheel figures stay Wheel White by day and Radium Lume by night at every value. The band shows only as the needle over the enamel, or the pen over the chart zones.

rules.name: The Lume Is Night Rule
rules.body: Only the night finish glows. The day finish has no glow anywhere, and the stale mark never glows in any finish. Stale is painted, not luminous. The day trace's soft edge is ink bleed, darker than the paper, not a glow.

rules.name: The Ink Follows the Ground Rule
rules.body: Day engraving takes its ink from the ground it is cut into, and night switches every ground to lume. Silver dial and chart paper take Engraver's Black. Brass (the aneroid bezel, the barograph housing bar) takes Bezel Umber over Relief Glint. The gunmetal plate takes Plate Cream, about 9.9 to 11.4:1. The stale mark follows the ground too: Stale Rust on silver, Light Ember on the day plate (7.5:1), Stale Ember on the night plate (6.5:1). Engraver's Black and Stale Rust never go on the plate.

rules.name: The Pen Ink Rule
rules.body: The day trace is ink from a pen, never a clean vector line. Each hourly segment is cut into steps of 1.3 pt or a little more, and every step except the segment's end is offset up to 0.28 pt along the normal, so the line still passes through every hourly reading. The offsets come from a generator seeded by the data, so the same 24 hours always draws the same line. The line is Violet Ink at 1.05 pt with round caps and joins, over a 2.3 pt bleed of the same ink at 28%, blurred 0.5 pt. At night the trace is a smooth 1.4 pt lume line with an 80% lume glow, radius 2 pt.

rules.name: The Engraver's Floor Rule
rules.body: Engraved text never drops below 9 pt. When space runs out, drop scale numerals first (the 50 already went), then shorten the legend. Never shrink. The floor sits two points under the iOS 11 pt guidance and holds only for tertiary engraving on the fixed-art face. App UI stays at 11 pt or above.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Each face has two type voices. The engraved serif sets every legend, numeral, time and inscription; Archivo Black sets the two readings on the wheels. A third voice, or the serif on a wheel, breaks the instrument.

rules.name: The 170 Grid Rule
rules.body: Author every aneroid measure in u = side / 170 and let the view scale. Only type has a floor.

rules.name: The 350 Canvas Rule
rules.body: Author every barograph measure in points on the 350 × 364 canvas and scale the finished face as one piece, never element by element. The chart window is measured off the housing art, and the plot, pen and chart labels are measured off the window, so the chart always sits inside the drum it is drawn on.

rules.name: The Raster Opening Rule
rules.body: The dial is a circle of radius 0.389 of the side at (0.498, 0.480). That matches the black opening in the `BezelTile` artwork, so the code dial covers it exactly. Move the dial and the plate's black shows.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Light comes from the upper left. Highlights sit up and left (dial sheen, crystal glare and crescent, hub cap gradient, plate bevel); shadows fall down and right (needle, hub, counters, screw heads, pen arm). Recesses invert: a counterbore lights its lower-right wall and a letter cut into the plate shades its upper-left wall. A new part lit from anywhere else is wrong.

rules.name: The Glass Over Everything Rule
rules.body: On the aneroid, the crystal is the top layer, and the needle, hub and counters sit under its glare. On the barograph the glass covers the drum only: paper, zones, grid and trace sit under it, and the housing, pen arm, engraving and counters sit above it. The accented finish has no glass on either size.

rules.name: The Raster Material, Code Data Rule
rules.body: A raster may carry a material and never a value. Brass, gunmetal, paper, glass, screws and the pen arm can be generated art; every zone, rule, label, trace point, figure and engraved string is drawn in code from the reading. A raster that moves with the data, like the pen arm, is placed by code and carries nothing that would need to change with it.

dos: Do measure every aneroid part in u = side / 170 and keep the dial at (0.498, 0.480) with radius 0.389 of the side.
Do measure every barograph part in points on the 350 × 364 canvas and place the plot, pen and labels from the housing's window.
Do keep the exact figures on the wheels and let the arc and the chart zones only place the band.

Do switch materials for night: lacquer face, black paper, lume ink with glow, `BezelTileNight` and the night barograph rasters, a gunmetal needle with a lume strip, the counter frame dimmed, the current enamel warmed 22% toward Lamp Warmth.
Do label each reading with its scale and source in the engraving (`PSI · 24H · CENTRAL`, `PSI · NEA 24H`, `AQI · WAQI`).
Do pick engraving ink by its ground: Engraver's Black on silver and paper, Bezel Umber on brass, Plate Cream on gunmetal, with the stale mark in Light Ember on the plate.
Do show missing data as blank wheels and a named failure in the legend, with the needle or pen parked at 0 when PSI is missing, and an engraved `TREND · <FAILURE>` on an empty chart.
Do peg the needle at 400 and let the counter show the true figure, up to 999.
Do build the hour axis from the data window, with the newest reading under the pen nib.
Do light every new part from the upper left and cast its shadow down and right.
Do put the needle, the pen, the trace and the wheel figures in the accent group, and drop the raster plate, screws, housing, paper, glass and crystal in the accented finish.
donts: Don't colour the figures, the counters or the plate by band. The thesis refuses the band-coloured number tile; the band lives in the enamel arc and the chart zones only.
Don't draw AQI on the arc or the chart, or give it a needle or a pen. The arc and the chart are NEA's PSI scale; AQI has its own counter.
Don't shrink engraved text below 9 pt. Drop numerals or shorten the legend instead.
Don't let anything glow by day, and don't let the stale mark glow at all.
Don't invent a figure to fill a wheel, or a trace to fill a chart. A blank wheel and an empty chart are the honest states.
Don't draw the day trace as a clean vector line, or let its wobble change between reloads of the same data.
Don't bake a value into a raster. Materials can be generated art; readings, zones, rules and labels are code.
Don't put icons, chips, cards or buttons on the face. Every mark is engraving, enamel, metal, paper, ink or glass.
